questions.question:
What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2040eaffb074fd42b592cdae119c98b95e1a291a924e7e0c4209b3005a60fec5.png] 

Given Equation: 32 − 15 ÷ 5 + 10 × 2 = ?

If ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged.

**New Equation: 32 + 15 × 5 − 10 ÷ 2 = ?**

32 + 15 × 5 − **__10 ÷ 2 __**= ?

32 + __**15 × 5**__ − 5 = ?

32 + 75 − 5 = ?

102.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**

questions.question: A machine depreciates at a rate of 10% per annum. If the current value of the machine is ₹1,00,000, what will be its value after 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of depreciation = 10% = 1/10.

Multiplying factor for each year = 1 − 1/10 = 9/10.

Value after 2 years = 1,00,000 × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ Value = 1,00,000 × 81/100 = 81,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹81,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Value (P) = ₹1,00,000

Rate of depreciation (R) = 10% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Current
 ₹1,00,000

 
• 
 −10%

 
 1 Year
 ₹90,000

 
• 
 −10%

 
 2 Years
 ₹81,000

 Successive Depreciation Method

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (1 − 10/100)²

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (90/100)²

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × 81/100

⇒ A = 1000 × 81 = 81,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹81,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Appreciation Formula

If an item appreciates in value at R% per annum, the value after n years is given by A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Change

For two consecutive percentage changes x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by (x + y + xy/100)%. For 10% depreciation twice, it is (−10 − 10 + 100/100)% = −19%. Value becomes 100% − 19% = 81% of the original.

Value n Years Ago

If the current value is P and it has been depreciating at R% per annum, its value n years ago was P ÷ (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: If the ratio of the quadrilateral's four angles is ∠w: ∠x: ∠y: ∠z = 2 : 3 : 3 : 4, then what is the value of ∠x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral is always 360°.

Total parts in the ratio = 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 12 parts.

12 parts = 360° ⇒ 1 part = 30°.

Value of ∠x = 3 parts = 3 × 30° = 90°.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of angles ∠w : ∠x : ∠y : ∠z = 2 : 3 : 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

 

 
 

 

 

 

 
 w (2k)
 x (3k)
 y (3k)
 z (4k)

 Sum of interior angles = 360°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the four angles be 2k, 3k, 3k, and 4k respectively.

⇒ ∠w + ∠x + ∠y + ∠z = 360°

⇒ 2k + 3k + 3k + 4k = 360°

⇒ 12k = 360°

⇒ k = 360° ÷ 12

⇒ k = 30°

⇒ The value of ∠x = 3k

⇒ ∠x = 3 × 30° = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of interior angles is calculated as (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral, it is (4 − 2) × 180° = 360°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, including a quadrilateral, is always 360° regardless of the number of sides.

Types of Quadrilaterals

If consecutive adjacent angles in a quadrilateral sum to 180°, the opposite sides are parallel. In this problem, ∠x + ∠y = 90° + 90° = 180°, meaning it forms a right-angled trapezium.

questions.question: In 1878, dissatisfied followers of Keshab Chandra Sen established the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj. Who among the following were its founders?

• Its primary founders were **Ananda Mohan Bose, Sib Chandra Deb, and Umesh Chandra Dutta**, who sought to uphold the democratic and liberal ideals of Brahmoism.
 
• The organization emphasized equality, rationalism, and monotheism, which were core tenets of the Brahmo faith.
 
• The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj also advocated for social reform, including the abolition of caste discrimination, child marriage, and promotion of women's education.
 
• This division marked a pivotal moment in the history of the Brahmo movement, leading to a more progressive and inclusive approach within the Samaj.

• It sought to promote rational thinking, social justice, and equality among all individuals.
 
 
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen:**
 
 
• A prominent Brahmo leader, Keshab Chandra Sen emphasized the need for spiritual and social reform.
 
• His leadership style and theological deviations led to the split within the Brahmo Samaj in 1878.

questions.question: Which of the following is the characteristic of Montane Forest?

options.text: Teak is the most dominant species of this forest.
Royal Bengal Tiger is the famous animal in these forests.
Evergreen broad-leaf trees, such as oaks and chestnuts predominate here.
Some of the important trees of this forest are ebony, mahogany etc.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evergreen broad-leaf trees, such as oaks and chestnuts predominate here.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Montane forests** are characterized by the presence of evergreen broad-leaf trees such as oaks, chestnuts, and other species adapted to cool and moist conditions.
 
• These forests are typically found in **hilly and mountainous regions**, especially at elevations ranging from 1000 to 3000 meters.
 
• They are known for their **dense canopy cover**, which supports a rich biodiversity including unique flora and fauna.
 
• Montane forests often experience **cooler temperatures and higher rainfall**, making them distinct from tropical forests.
 
• The vegetation in montane forests changes with altitude, ranging from evergreen forests at lower elevations to coniferous forests at higher altitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montane Ecosystem:**

 
 
• This ecosystem is associated with mountainous regions and is highly influenced by altitude, climate, and soil types.
 
• It supports a variety of flora and fauna, including species that are endemic to these regions.
 
 
 
• **Altitudinal Zonation:**
 
 
• The vegetation in montane forests varies by altitude, transitioning from tropical forests at lower elevations to alpine vegetation at higher altitudes.
 
• Common zones include tropical montane forests, temperate montane forests, and alpine meadows.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Influence:**
 
 
• Montane forests are typically found in areas with cool and moist climates.
 
• They play a crucial role in regulating water cycles and preventing soil erosion in mountainous regions.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity:**
 
 
• Montane forests are home to a wide variety of plants and animals, including many rare and endangered species.
 
• The unique climate and elevation make these forests a biodiversity hotspot.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles deals with the composition of the panchayats?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Article 243C** deals with the composition of Panchayats in India as per the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
 
• The composition of Panchayats includes directly elected members at the village, intermediate, and district levels.
 
• It mandates that the Chairperson of a Panchayat at the village level is elected as per the procedure established by state legislation.
 
• It provides flexibility to states to determine the representation of members, reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women, and other relevant details.
 
• Reservation of seats in every Panchayat is done according to Articles 243D and 243T, ensuring inclusivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:**

 
 
• Introduced Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) in India to promote decentralized governance.
 
• Added Part IX to the Constitution and Articles 243 to 243O.
 
• Mandates a three-tier system: Village, Intermediate, and District levels.
 
 
 
• **Article 243A:**
 
 
• Empowers Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• The Gram Sabha comprises all registered voters within a village Panchayat's jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Article 243B:**
 
 
• Provides for the establishment of Panchayats at various levels in every state.
 
• States have the discretion to decide whether to establish Panchayats at the intermediate level based on population.
 
 
 
• **Article 243D:**
 
 
• Mandates reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women in Panchayats.
 
• Reservation for women is not less than one-third of the total seats.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj:**
 
 
• It is a system of governance at the rural level to ensure grassroots democracy.

questions.question: The Brundtland Report, 'Our Common Future' (1987), formally introduced which key concept, defined as meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sustainable Development**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of **Sustainable Development** was formally introduced in the Brundtland Report, titled Our Common Future*, published in 1987 by the United Nations World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED).
 
• Sustainable development is defined as **"development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs."**
 
• The Brundtland Report highlighted the interconnectedness of economic, social, and environmental dimensions, emphasizing the need for a balance between these factors to ensure long-term global sustainability.
 
• It paved the way for major international agreements and frameworks, such as the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, which were adopted in 2015.
 
• The report brought global attention to critical issues like environmental degradation, social inequality, and the need for sustainable resource management.

***Additional Information__**

 
• **Brundtland Commission:**

 
 
• Also known as the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), it was established by the United Nations in 1983.
 
• The commission was chaired by **Gro Harlem Brundtland**, the former Prime Minister of Norway, hence the name.
 
• Its objective was to address the growing concern about environmental degradation and its impact on economic and social development.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The SDGs are a set of **17 interconnected global goals** adopted by the UN in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
 
• They aim to eradicate poverty, combat climate change, and promote economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability.
 
• Examples of SDGs include Goal 13 (Climate Action), Goal 1 (No Poverty), and Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy).
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of Sustainable Development:**
 
 
• Intergenerational Equity: Ensuring that resources are available for future generations.
 
• Integration: Balancing environmental, social, and economic factors in decision-making.
 
• Precautionary Principle: Taking preventive action to protect the environment, even in the absence of full scientific certainty.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**
 
 
• The Brundtland Report inspired the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, where nations adopted the Agenda 21*, a comprehensive plan for sustainable development.
 
• It also influenced the creation of the **Paris Agreement** in 2015, aimed at combating climate change and limiting global temperature rise.

questions.question: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Gandhi’s first major involvement in India’s freedom struggle, was launched in support of which group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigo farmers in Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha of 1917** marked Mahatma Gandhi’s first major involvement in India’s freedom struggle.
 
• It was launched in support of **Indigo farmers in Bihar**, who were oppressed under the exploitative tinkathia system.
 
• The farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at fixed prices, leading to severe financial hardship.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi’s intervention in Champaran was aimed at addressing the farmers' grievances and demonstrating the power of nonviolent resistance.
 
• The success of the Champaran movement brought attention to the plight of farmers and strengthened Gandhi’s leadership in the national movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tinkathia System:**

 
 
• Under this system, farmers were forced to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land, regardless of their own preferences.
 
• The system was exploitative and caused significant economic distress for the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Role of Gandhi:**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi visited Champaran in 1917 after being requested by local leaders like Raj Kumar Shukla.
 
• He adopted the method of Satyagraha (nonviolent resistance) to address the injustice faced by farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Movement:**
 
 
• The movement led to the abolition of the tinkathia system and improved the condition of farmers in the region.
 
• It demonstrated the effectiveness of nonviolent resistance and became a precursor to future freedom struggles under Gandhi’s leadership.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Cultivation:**
 
 
• Indigo was a dye plant that was in high demand in Europe during colonial times.
 
• The forced cultivation of indigo caused soil depletion, which further impacted farmers’ livelihoods.

questions.question: The marked price of a shirt is ₹1,200. A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 5% and 15% on the marked price. By how many rupees is the selling price less than the marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The amount by which the Selling Price is less than the Marked Price is simply the Total Discount.

Effective percentage of two successive discounts (5% and 15%) = 5 + 15 − (5 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective discount = 20 − 0.75 = 19.25%

Total Discount Amount = 19.25% of ₹1200

⇒ Total Discount = (19.25 ÷ 100) × 1200 = ₹231

**∴ The correct answer is ₹231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1200

First successive discount (D₁) = 5%

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a direct tax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Value Added Tax (VAT)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Value Added Tax (VAT)** is an indirect tax levied on goods and services at each stage of production or distribution, based on the value added at that stage.
 
• It is collected by businesses on behalf of the government and is included in the price paid by consumers, making it an indirect tax.
 
• Unlike direct taxes such as income tax or corporate tax, VAT is not paid directly by individuals but is included in the price of goods and services.
 
• Direct taxes, such as income tax, corporate tax, and tax on capital gains, are paid directly by individuals or entities to the government based on their income or earnings.
 
• The primary difference lies in the point of incidence: direct taxes are levied on income/profits, while indirect taxes like VAT are levied on consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct Taxes:**

 
 
• Direct taxes are levied directly on the income or wealth of individuals, companies, or other entities.
 
• Examples include income tax, corporate tax, and capital gains tax.
 
• These taxes are progressive, meaning higher income earners pay a larger proportion.
 
 
 
• **Indirect Taxes:**
 
 
• Indirect taxes are levied on goods and services, and the burden is passed on to the final consumer.
 
• Examples include VAT, Goods and Services Tax (GST), excise duty, and customs duty.
 
• These taxes are regressive, as all consumers, regardless of their income level, pay the same rate.
 
 
 
• **Value Added Tax (VAT):**
 
 
• VAT is a consumption tax placed on a product whenever value is added at any stage of the supply chain.
 
• It is implemented in most countries, but India now uses Goods and Services Tax (GST), which subsumes VAT.
 
• VAT ensures tax collection at multiple points in the production and distribution process.
 
 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST):**
 
 
• GST replaced VAT and other indirect taxes in India in July 2017.
 
• It is a unified tax system that simplifies indirect taxation by combining multiple taxes into one.
 
• GST is categorized into CGST, SGST, and IGST, based on intrastate and interstate transactions.

questions.question: Simplify: 0.848 ÷ 0.8 × (1)/(2) + 0.125 ÷ (5)/(2) × 0.4

__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the BODMAS rule directly to the expression to solve division first, then multiplication, then addition.

Part 1: 0.848 ÷ 0.8 × 1/2 = 1.06 × 0.5 = 0.53

Part 2: 0.125 ÷ 5/2 × 0.4 = 0.125 × 2/5 × 0.4 = 0.05 × 0.4 = 0.02

Total = 0.53 + 0.02 = 0.55

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 0.848 ÷ 0.8 × 1/2 + 0.125 ÷ 5/2 × 0.4

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ (0.848 ÷ 0.8) × 1/2 + (0.125 ÷ 2.5) × 0.4

⇒ 1.06 × 0.5 + 0.05 × 0.4

⇒ 0.53 + 0.02

⇒ 0.55

**∴ The correct answer is 0.55.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The rule dictates the order of operations: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Dividing by Fractions

To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal. Example: A ÷ (B/C) = A × (C/B).

Decimal Multiplication

Multiply as whole numbers, then position the decimal point so the total decimal places match the sum of decimal places in the multiplied numbers.

questions.question:
Which of the following are aspects of the Centre-State legislative relation?

1. Territorial extent of Central and state legislation

2. Distribution of legislative subjects

3. Parliamentary legislation in the state field

4. Centre’s control over state legislation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2, 3 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The legislative relations between the Centre and States in India are governed by Part XI of the Constitution, specifically Articles 245 to 255.
 
• **Territorial extent of legislation:** Article 245 specifies the extent of laws made by the Parliament and the State Legislatures within their respective territories.
 
• **Distribution of legislative subjects:** The Constitution lists subjects under the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List (Schedule VII), assigning legislative powers accordingly.
 
• **Parliamentary legislation in state matters:** Articles 249, 250, and 252 allow Parliament to legislate on matters in the State List under special circumstances like national interest or state consent.
 
• **Centre's control over state legislation:** Article 254 ensures that in case of conflict between a state law and central law on a Concurrent List subject, the central law prevails.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects on which only the Parliament can legislate, including defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, etc.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects on which State Legislatures have exclusive power to legislate, such as police, public health, agriculture, etc.
 
• **Concurrent List:** Includes subjects like education, marriage, trade unions, etc., where both the Centre and States can make laws. However, central law prevails in case of conflict.
 
• **Residuary Powers:** Matters not enumerated in any of the lists fall under the purview of the Parliament as per Article 248.
 
• **President's role:** State legislation on certain matters may require the President’s assent, especially if it affects the Centre-State legislative framework.

questions.question: What happens to the speed of sound in a medium when its temperature increases?

options.text: It is not affected by the temperature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The s**peed of sound in a medium increases with the rise in temperature because the molecules of the medium move faster**, enhancing the transmission of sound waves.
 
• In gases, the speed of sound is directly proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature (**v ∝ √T**), as per the formula **v = √(γRT/M)**, where T is the temperature in Kelvin.
 
• An increase in temperature reduces the density of the medium, which also contributes to the increased speed of sound.
 
• For **every 1°C rise in temperature**, the **speed of sound in air increases by approximately** **0.6 m/s**.
 
• The relationship between speed of sound and temperature is particularly significant in gases but less pronounced in liquids and solids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Sound:**

 
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium through which it travels: it is fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• For example, in air at 20°C, the speed of sound is approximately 343 m/s, while in water, it is around 1,480 m/s, and in steel, it is about 5,960 m/s.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures lead to a higher speed of sound due to increased molecular activity.
 
• **Density:** Lower density usually results in higher speeds in gases, while in solids and liquids, the relationship is more complex.
 
• **Elasticity:** A medium with higher elasticity transmits sound faster.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Speed of Sound in Gases:**
 
 
• The formula is **v = √(γRT/M)**, where:
 
 
• **γ:** Adiabatic index (ratio of specific heats).
 
• **R:** Universal gas constant.
 
• **T:** Absolute temperature in Kelvin.
 
• **M:** Molar mass of the gas.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding the speed of sound is crucial in fields like meteorology, aviation, and acoustics.
 
• The temperature dependence of sound speed is used in weather forecasting and studying atmospheric layers.

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a surface phenomenon where particles at the s**urface of a liquid absorb energy and change into the gaseous state**.
 
• During evaporation, particles absorb latent heat from their surroundings, which lowers the temperature of the surroundings and causes cooling.
 
• **Latent heat is the energy required for a substance to change its state without a change in its temperature**.
 
• Evaporation occurs faster in conditions such as higher temperature, increased surface area, lower humidity, and faster wind speed.
 
• This cooling effect is commonly observed in daily life, such as sweating, where evaporation helps regulate body temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latent Heat:**

• Types include latent heat of fusion (solid to liquid) and latent heat of vaporization (liquid to gas).
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**
 
 
• Temperature: Higher temperatures increase the rate of evaporation.
 
• Surface Area: Larger surface areas allow more particles to evaporate simultaneously.
 
• Humidity: Lower humidity increases evaporation as the air can hold more water vapor.
 
• Wind Speed: Faster winds remove water vapor from the surface, enhancing evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation is used in cooling systems like air coolers and refrigerators.
 
• It plays a key role in the water cycle, contributing to cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• Industrial processes such as salt extraction rely on evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation vs Boiling:**
 
 
• Evaporation occurs at any temperature and only at the surface of the liquid.
 
• Boiling occurs at a specific temperature (boiling point) and throughout the liquid.

• The name **Panthalassa** is derived from Greek, meaning "all sea" (*pan* = all, *thalassa* = sea).
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping Earth's climate and ocean currents during the time of Pangaea’s existence, approximately 335 to 175 million years ago.
 
• As Pangaea began to break apart, Panthalassa gradually transformed into the Pacific Ocean, the largest ocean on Earth today.

• A column width of 1 equals the width of one digit of the default font size, typically Arial 10-point.
 
• Although the column width is limited to 255, the cell content can still store up to **32,767 characters**, but not all will be visible without adjusting column width or using text wrapping.

• The maximum row height in MS Excel is **409 points**.
 
• This measurement is based on the height of characters in the default font size.
 
 
 
• **Cell Character Limit:**
 
 
• Each cell in MS Excel can store a maximum of **32,767 characters**.
 
• However, only 1,024 characters are visible in a cell unless text wrapping or merging is applied.
 
 
 
• **Pixel and Point Relationship:**
 
 
• A point is a unit of measurement equivalent to 1/72 of an inch.
 
• Pixels represent the resolution of a display, and their size varies depending on the monitor's DPI (dots per inch).

• Column width can be adjusted manually by dragging the column boundary or automatically using the "AutoFit Column Width" feature.
 
• AutoFit adjusts the column width to fit the longest entry in the column.
 
 
 
• **Excel Default Settings:**
 
 
• The default column width in Excel is **8.43**, which equals the width of 8 characters in the default font.
 
• The default row height is **15 points**, sufficient to display a single line of text in the default font size.

questions.question: The primary force responsible for pulling water upward in tall plants is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transpiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water evaporates from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through the stomata present in leaves.
 
• The evaporation of water creates a negative pressure or suction force, known as the **transpiration pull**, which helps to draw water upward through the xylem vessels.
 
• Transpiration plays a crucial role in maintaining the flow of water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
 
• This process is most significant in tall plants, where the force generated by transpiration pull is essential to overcome gravity and transport water to the top.
 
• Environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, wind, and light intensity influence the rate of transpiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is the vascular tissue responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• It consists of specialized cells such as tracheids and vessel elements that facilitate the movement of water.
 
• The cohesion and adhesion properties of water molecules play a key role in maintaining the continuous water column in xylem vessels.
 
 
 
• **Root Pressure**
 
 
• Root pressure is a positive pressure generated by the active absorption of nutrients and water by root cells.
 
• Although root pressure contributes to water movement, it is insufficient for tall plants and is only effective in smaller plants.
 
 
 
• **Guttation**
 
 
• Guttation is the exudation of water droplets from the edges of leaves, typically occurring at night or under conditions of high soil moisture and low transpiration.
 
• It should not be confused with transpiration, which is the evaporation of water vapor from plant surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Osmosis**
 
 
• Osmosis is the passive movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of low solute concentration to a region of high solute concentration.
 
• While osmosis is critical for water absorption by root cells, it does not contribute to the upward movement of water in tall plants.

questions.question: The value of 6²+sqrt{2²}-5sqrt{25}-11 is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve directly by expanding powers and roots using BODMAS:

⇒ 6² + √(2²) − 5√25 − 11

⇒ 36 + 2 − 5 × 5 − 11

⇒ 38 − 25 − 11

⇒ 38 − 36 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 6² + √(2²) − 5√25 − 11

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Evaluate the powers and roots first (Orders):

⇒ 6² = 36

⇒ √(2²) = √4 = 2

⇒ √25 = 5

⇒ Substitute these evaluated terms back into the main expression:

⇒ 36 + 2 − 5 × 5 − 11

⇒ Perform multiplication:

⇒ 36 + 2 − 25 − 11

⇒ Perform addition and subtraction from left to right:

⇒ 38 − 25 − 11

⇒ 38 − 36

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The fundamental order of mathematical operations is Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Perfect Squares and Roots

Memorizing basic squares up to 30 significantly helps speed up simplification calculations. For instance, the principal square root of x² is x for any positive number.

Simplifying Multiple Subtractions

When an expression contains multiple numbers to be subtracted consecutively, you can add all the negative terms first and then subtract the sum. For example, −25 − 11 = −(25 + 11) = −36.
</p

questions.question: The reservation of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions is provided by which of the following Constitutional amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73rd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, passed in 1992, introduced provisions for **the establishment of Panchayati Raj institutions** in India.
 
• It mandated the **reservation of one-third of seats** for women, including the position of chairpersons, in Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• This amendment added **Part IX** to the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," and a new Schedule, **Schedule XI**, enumerating 29 subjects under the Panchayati Raj's jurisdiction.
 
• The amendment aimed at empowering women and ensuring their active participation in local self-governance.
 
• The reservation for women was designed to enhance **political representation and decision-making** capabilities for women in rural governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IX of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Part IX was introduced through the 73rd Amendment, focusing on rural self-governance through Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• The Gram Sabha serves as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• It stipulates a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
 
 
• **Reservation for Women in Local Governance:**
 
 
• The provision for reservation of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions aims to **enhance women's representation in politics.**
 
• One-third of the total seats, including the positions of chairpersons, are reserved for women across all levels.
 
• This reservation is applicable to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as well.
 
 
 
• **Schedule XI:**
 
 
• It lists 29 functional items that Panchayati Raj institutions are responsible for, such as agriculture, education, health, sanitation, and rural development.
 
• These subjects enable decentralized governance and decision-making at the local level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 73rd Amendment:**
 
 
• It strengthened grassroots democracy and decentralized governance.
 
• The amendment empowered marginalized groups, including women, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes, to participate in governance.
 
• This institutionalized local self-government, making it a constitutional mandate.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution automatically suspends the Fundamental Rights during emergencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 358**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 358 of the Indian Constitution provides for the automatic suspension of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 during a National Emergency.
 
• It applies only when the emergency is proclaimed due to war or external aggression (not in cases of internal disturbance).
 
• During such emergencies, legislative and executive actions violating Article 19 cannot be challenged in a court of law.
 
• Article 358 ceases to operate once the Emergency ends, and Article 19 is automatically restored.
 
• Only rights under Article 19 are affected; other Fundamental Rights remain enforceable unless specifically suspended under Article 359.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 359:**

 
 
• Allows the President to suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21) during a National Emergency.
 
• Unlike Article 358, Article 359 requires a specific presidential order for suspension.
 
 
 
• **Article 352:**
 
 
• Deals with the proclamation of National Emergency in case of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It forms the constitutional basis for invoking Articles 358 and 359 during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, guaranteeing essential rights to Indian citizens.
 
• Key rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right to Constitutional Remedies, etc.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The suspension of Fundamental Rights under Articles 358 and 359 was notably applied during the Emergency of 1975-77.
 
• The Emergency was declared under Article 352 due to "internal disturbance," later amended to "armed rebellion" by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

questions.question: Three bells ring at intervals of 12, 15 and 18 minutes. If they rang together at 10:00 am, when will they ring together again?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The bells will ring together again after the LCM of their individual intervals.

LCM of 12, 15, and 18 = 180 minutes.

180 minutes = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours.

Next ringing time = 10:00 a.m. + 3 hours = 1:00 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:00 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Intervals of the three bells = 12, 15, and 18 minutes.

Initial simultaneous ringing time = 10:00 a.m.

**Concept Used:**

The time after which all bells will ring together again is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their individual time intervals.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ LCM(12, 15, 18) = Highest power of all prime factors = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180

⇒ Thus, the bells will ring together after 180 minutes.

⇒ Converting minutes into hours: 180 minutes = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours

⇒ Next time they ring together = 10:00 a.m. + 3 hours = 1:00 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:00 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM in Real-Life Scenarios

LCM is used to find when different events running at different regular intervals will coincide again, such as bells ringing, traffic lights changing, or runners meeting on a circular track.

HCF vs LCM

HCF (Highest Common Factor) is used to split items into smaller equal sections or to distribute things equally, whereas LCM (Least Common Multiple) is used to find a common future event.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two given numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).
</p

questions.question: In the context of operating systems, what does PCB stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Process Control Block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Process Control Block (PCB) is a data structure in the operating system that stores information about a process.
 
• PCB contains important details such as the process ID, process state, program counter, CPU registers, memory management information, and I/O status.
 
• It is used by the operating system to track and manage processes during execution.
 
• Whenever a context switch occurs, the PCB ensures that the state of the process is saved and restored correctly.
 
• The operating system maintains a PCB for each process to efficiently manage multitasking and resource allocation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 70 cm, 56 cm and 42 cm. What is its area? (in cm² )

Ratio of the sides = 42 : 56 : 70 = 3 : 4 : 5.

Since the ratio of the sides follows the Pythagorean triplet (3² + 4² = 5²), the given triangle is a right-angled triangle.

Area of a right-angled triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height.

Where s = Semi-perimeter = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 39?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by 39, it must be divisible by its co-prime factors 3 and 13.

Check divisibility by 3: The sum of digits for 625092 is 6 + 2 + 5 + 0 + 9 + 2 = 24 (Divisible by 3).

Check divisibility by 13: The difference of alternating 3-digit blocks for 625092 is |625 − 092| = 533.

Since 533 ÷ 13 = 41, it is perfectly divisible by 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 625092.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Options provided: 625649, 622710, 625092, 622776

**Formula Used:**

Divisibility by 39 = Divisibility by both 3 and 13.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, check divisibility by 3 (the sum of all digits must be a multiple of 3).

⇒ 625649: 6 + 2 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 9 = 32 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ 622710: 6 + 2 + 2 + 7 + 1 + 0 = 18 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 625092: 6 + 2 + 5 + 0 + 9 + 2 = 24 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 622776: 6 + 2 + 2 + 7 + 7 + 6 = 30 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ Next, check divisibility by 13 for the remaining valid options (difference between alternating 3-digit blocks must be a multiple of 13).

⇒ 622710: |710 − 622| = 88 → 88 is not divisible by 13.

⇒ 625092: |092 − 625| = 533 → 533 ÷ 13 = 41 (Divisible by 13)

⇒ 622776: |776 − 622| = 154 → 154 is not divisible by 13.

⇒ Only 625092 fully satisfies both conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is 625092.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Factor Rule

If a given number is perfectly divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, it is guaranteed to be divisible by their product (a × b).

Divisibility by 13

Group the digits in sets of three starting from right to left. If the absolute difference of the alternating sums of these groups is 0 or a multiple of 13, the complete number is divisible by 13.

Divisibility by 7, 11, and 13

The 3-digit block alternating difference method works identically for 7, 11, and 13 since their product is exactly 1001.
</p

questions.question: The average of three numbers is 49. The first number is twice the second, and the second is twice the third. What is the largest number?

Total sum = Average × 3 = 49 × 3 = 147.

Ratio of First : Second : Third = 4 : 2 : 1.

Total ratio parts = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 parts.

7 parts = 147 ⇒ 1 part = 21.

Largest number (4 parts) = 4 × 21 = 84.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Sum of observations = Average × Total number of observations

⇒ First number = 2 × 2x = 4x.

⇒ Sum of the three numbers = 49 × 3 = 147.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Snell's law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is constant for a given pair of media and is equal to the refractive index.
 
• The mathematical expression for Snell's law is **sin i ÷ sin r = n**, where **n** is the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.
 
• This law explains the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another with a different refractive index.
 
• Snell's law is crucial in understanding optical phenomena such as refraction and total internal reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refractive Index (n):**

 
 
• The refractive index is a dimensionless quantity that describes how light propagates through a medium.
 
• It is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the medium: **n = c/v**.
 
 
 
• **Angle of Incidence (i):**

• **Angle of Refraction (r):**

• **Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, causing the light to reflect entirely within the denser medium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Used in designing lenses, prisms, and optical instruments like microscopes and telescopes.
 
• Essential in fiber optic communication for guiding light signals through cables.

questions.question: Which Governor-General of India (1848-1856) was mainly associated with enforcing the Doctrine of Lapse to annex Indian states without a male heir?

__
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** served as the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• He is best known for implementing the **Doctrine of Lapse**, a policy used to annex Indian states that lacked a legitimate male heir.
 
• Under this doctrine, princely states like **Satara (1848), Jhansi (1854), and Nagpur (1853)** were annexed by the British Empire.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was a controversial policy as it disregarded the traditional right of rulers to adopt heirs, leading to widespread discontent among Indian rulers.

• **Doctrine of Lapse:**

 
 
• A policy formulated by Lord Dalhousie, stating that if a ruler of a princely state died without a direct male heir, his state would "lapse" to the British Empire.
 
• This doctrine overrode the traditional rights of rulers to adopt heirs and was viewed as a coercive measure to expand British territories.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Dalhousie's Policies:**
 
 
• Dalhousie's policies led to the expansion of British territory but also increased dissatisfaction among Indian rulers and subjects.
 
• The annexations under the Doctrine of Lapse were a significant factor contributing to the **Indian Revolt of 1857.**
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions of Lord Dalhousie:**
 
 
• Dalhousie introduced modern infrastructure like railways, telegraphs, and postal services in India.
 
• He established English-medium education institutions and laid the foundation for modernization in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Revolt of 1857:**
 
 
• The widespread discontent caused by annexation policies, including the Doctrine of Lapse, was one of the primary reasons for the revolt.
 
• The revolt marked the beginning of the end of the East India Company's rule, leading to the establishment of direct British governance in India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Citizenship in India** is covered under **Articles 5 to 11** of the Constitution of India and deals with the different categories of persons who are entitled to citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Citizenship is** not listed in the State List**; it is in the** Union List under the Seventh Schedule**, making it a subject under the exclusive jurisdiction of the central government.
 
• Indian citizenship can be acquired through **five ways: birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory,** as per the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• The Constitution provided initial provisions for citizenship, and subsequent changes have been made through amendments to the Citizenship Act.
 
• Correct statement here is "Articles 5 to 11 deal with various categories of persons entitled to citizenship," which aligns with the provisions in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Citizenship Act, 1955**

 
 
• This Act governs the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship.
 
• It lays down five modes of acquiring citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• It also provides provisions for the termination and renunciation of citizenship.
 
 
 
• **Union List vs State List**
 
 
• The Union List contains subjects of national importance on which only the central government can make laws, including citizenship, defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy.
 
• State List contains matters on which state governments can legislate, such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Dual Citizenship**
 
 
• India does not allow dual citizenship. Indian citizens cannot hold citizenship of another country simultaneously.
 
• However, the Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) status provides certain rights to foreign nationals of Indian origin.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to Citizenship Act**
 
 
• The Citizenship Act has been amended several times, including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, which provides citizenship to persecuted minorities from Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
 
• This amendment has sparked debates around secularism and equality in India.

Combine terms with the same denominator first: 5/2 − 3/2 = 2/2 = 1

Simplify the complex fraction: 1 / (1 + 5/7) = 1 / (12/7) = 7/12

⇒ 5/2 + 7/12 − 3/2

⇒ 2/2 + 7/12

⇒ (12 + 7) / 12

• **text/plain** is the default MIME Content-Type for plain text email messages.
 
• The **charset=UTF-8** specification ensures support for a wide range of characters, including international ones.
 
• MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) standards define how email content is formatted and transmitted.
 
• Plain text emails are simple and do not contain formatting, such as bold or italic text, images, or hyperlinks.
 
• Plain text is widely used for compatibility across email clients and platforms, ensuring readability.

**Given:**

⇒ Speeds for three equal distances: S₁ = 19 km/hr, S₂ = 8 km/hr, S₃ = 5 km/hr.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 Speed: 19 km/hr
 Speed: 8 km/hr
 Speed: 5 km/hr

 Time = d/19
 Time = d/8
 Time = d/5

 Total Distance = 3d

questions.question: Which meristematic tissue is found at nodes and helps in regrowth of grasses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intercalary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Intercalary meristem is a type of meristematic tissue located at the nodes of plants.
 
• It is responsible for the regrowth of grasses and contributes to the elongation of internodes.
 
• Intercalary meristems allow rapid regeneration in grasses after grazing or mowing.
 
• This tissue is present in monocots, particularly in grasses, which aids their survival in environments with regular disturbances.
 
• Unlike apical meristem, which is found at the tips of roots and shoots, intercalary meristem is strategically located at the base of nodes and leaf blades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Meristematic tissues are responsible for the growth of plants and consist of actively dividing cells.
 
• These tissues are classified into apical, lateral, and intercalary based on their location.
 
• Apical meristem contributes to the primary growth at the tips of roots and shoots.
 
• Lateral meristem is involved in secondary growth, leading to an increase in the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Monocots vs. Dicots:**
 
 
• Monocots, like grasses, have intercalary meristems that help them regrow quickly after damage.
 
• Dicots generally lack intercalary meristems and rely on apical and lateral meristems for growth.
 
 
 
• **Node and Internode:**
 
 
• Nodes are points on the stem where leaves or branches originate.
 
• Internodes are the regions between two nodes, which elongate due to intercalary meristem activity.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation in Grasses:**
 
 
• Grasses are adapted to survive grazing, fire, or mowing due to the presence of intercalary meristems.
 
• These tissues regenerate leaf blades and stems quickly, ensuring survival and growth.

Final value in percentage = 0.735075 × 100% = 73.5075%

questions.question: In the substitution of methane with chlorine, sunlight is required to:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sunlight provides energy in the form of ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which is essential to break the bond between chlorine molecules (Cl₂) and initiate the process of free radical formation.
 
• Free radicals are highly reactive species required for the chain reaction of methane substitution.
 
• The reaction begins with the homolytic cleavage of chlorine (Cl₂) under the influence of UV light, producing chlorine free radicals.
 
• These chlorine free radicals attack methane (CH₄), leading to the formation of methyl radicals and hydrogen chloride (HCl).
 
• This chain reaction results in successive substitutions where methane reacts with chlorine to form chlorinated products such as chloromethane, dichloromethane, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Radical:**

 
 
• A free radical is an atom or molecule that contains an unpaired electron, making it highly reactive.
 
• In chemical reactions, free radicals play a crucial role in initiating chain processes.
 
 
 
• **Homolytic Cleavage:**
 
 
• Homolytic cleavage refers to the breaking of a bond where each atom retains one electron, forming two free radicals.
 
• This process is often facilitated by UV light or heat.
 
 
 
• **Substitution Reaction:**
 
 
• Substitution reactions involve the replacement of one atom or group in a molecule with another atom or group.
 
• In this case, chlorine atoms replace hydrogen atoms in methane during the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Photochemical Reaction:**
 
 
• A photochemical reaction is initiated by the absorption of light energy, typically UV or visible light.
 
• The substitution of methane with chlorine is a classic example of a photochemical reaction.
 
 
 
• **Reaction Products:**
 
 
• Depending on the extent of substitution, products such as chloromethane (CH₃Cl), dichloromethane (CH₂Cl₂), trichloromethane (CHCl₃), and tetrachloromethane(CHCl3) can be formed.

questions.question: if x varies inversely as y³ - 1 and x is equal to 6 when y = 4, find the value of x when y = 8.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For inverse variation, the product of the variables remains constant.

⇒ x₁ × (y₁³ − 1) = x₂ × (y₂³ − 1)

⇒ 6 × (4³ − 1) = x × (8³ − 1)

⇒ 6 × 63 = x × 511

⇒ x = 378 ÷ 511 = 54/73

**∴ The correct answer is 54/73.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x varies inversely as (y³ − 1).

When x = 6, y = 4.

**Formula Used:**

If A is inversely proportional to B, then A = k ÷ B, where k is a constant.

 Inverse Variation: x × (y³ − 1) = Constant
 
 
 State 1

 y₁³ − 1 = 63

 x₂ = ?
 y₂ = 8
 y₂³ − 1 = 511
 
 6 × 63 = x₂ × 511

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = k ÷ (y³ − 1)

⇒ 6 = k ÷ (4³ − 1)

⇒ 6 = k ÷ (64 − 1)

⇒ k = 6 × 63 = 378

Now, substitute y = 8 to find the new value of x:

⇒ x = 378 ÷ (8³ − 1)

⇒ x = 378 ÷ (512 − 1)

⇒ x = 378 ÷ 511

Divide both the numerator and the denominator by their common factor, 7:

⇒ x = (7 × 54) ÷ (7 × 73)

⇒ x = 54/73

**∴ The correct answer is 54/73.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

If two quantities vary directly, their ratio is constant: A ÷ B = k or A = k × B.

Inverse Variation

If two quantities vary inversely, their product is constant: A × B = k or A = k ÷ B.

questions.question: What does the number of compressions or rarefactions passing a point per unit time represent in a sound wave?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Frequency refers to the number of compressions or rarefactions passing a given point per unit time in a sound wave.
 
• It is typically measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, which represents cycles per second.
 
• High-frequency sound waves correspond to a high pitch, while low-frequency sound waves correspond to a low pitch.
 
• The frequency of a sound wave determines its tone, distinguishing one sound from another.
 
• In physics, frequency is an essential parameter in the study of wave phenomena, including sound and electromagnetic waves.

• It is related to the loudness of the sound—the greater the amplitude, the louder the sound.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength**:
 
 
• Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions in a sound wave.
 
• It is inversely proportional to frequency: higher frequency means shorter wavelength.
 
 
 
• **Loudness**:
 
 
• Loudness is a subjective measure of sound intensity perceived by the human ear.
 
• It is influenced by both the amplitude of the sound wave and the sensitivity of the listener's ear.
 
 
 
• **Sound Wave Basics**:
 
 
• Sound waves are longitudinal waves that propagate through a medium by compressing and rarefying particles.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium's properties, such as density and elasticity.

• Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture approximately **1% of the solar energy** that falls on their leaves and convert it into chemical energy via photosynthesis.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following.

(4)/(3)+((1)/(1+frac{2){7}})-(4)/(3)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Notice that the term 4/3 appears as both positive and negative in the given expression.

Cancel out +4/3 and −4/3 directly to save time.

The expression immediately reduces to 1 ÷ (1 + 2/7).

Solve the denominator: 1 + 2/7 = 9/7.

The reciprocal of 9/7 is 7/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/9.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 4/3 + [1 ÷ (1 + 2/7)] − 4/3

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS Rule: Solve brackets first, followed by division, addition, and subtraction.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let E = 4/3 + [1 ÷ (1 + 2/7)] − 4/3

⇒ First, simplify the term inside the inner parenthesis: 1 + 2/7

⇒ 1 + 2/7 = (7 + 2) / 7 = 9/7

⇒ Now, substitute this result back into the main expression:

⇒ E = 4/3 + [1 ÷ (9/7)] − 4/3

⇒ Dividing 1 by a fraction gives its reciprocal. So, 1 ÷ (9/7) = 7/9

⇒ E = 4/3 + 7/9 − 4/3

⇒ Rearranging the terms to group like fractions: E = (4/3 − 4/3) + 7/9

⇒ E = 0 + 7/9 = 7/9

**∴ The correct answer is 7/9.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It sets the standard sequence of operations for evaluating mathematical expressions correctly.

Reciprocal of a Fraction

The reciprocal of a fraction a/b is b/a. It is mathematically equivalent to dividing 1 by the fraction: 1 ÷ (a/b) = b/a.

Addition and Subtraction of Fractions

When adding or subtracting fractions with identical denominators, you can directly add or subtract the numerators while keeping the denominator the same.

questions.question: The number 977340 is divisible by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by 35 if it is divisible by its co-prime factors 5 and 7.

The number 977340 ends in 0, so it is clearly divisible by 5.

Applying the 7 divisibility rule (difference of alternate triplets): 977 − 340 = 637.

Since 637 is completely divisible by 7 (637 ÷ 7 = 91), the original number is divisible by 7.

Hence, the number is divisible by 5 × 7 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 977340

**To check:**

Which among 24, 35, 37, 34 divides 977340 completely.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's check 24: A number is divisible by 24 if it is divisible by both 3 and 8.

⇒ The last 3 digits are 340. 340 is not divisible by 8, so 977340 is not divisible by 24.

⇒ Let's check 35: A number is divisible by 35 if it is divisible by both 5 and 7.

⇒ Unit digit is 0, so it is divisible by 5.

⇒ To check for 7, divide the number directly: 977340 ÷ 7 = 139620 (Remainder is 0).

⇒ Since it is divisible by both 5 and 7, it is divisible by 35.

⇒ Checking 34 (17 × 2): 977340 ÷ 17 gives a remainder of 10, so it is not divisible.

⇒ Checking 37: 977340 ÷ 37 gives a remainder of 22, so it is not divisible.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11, and 13

If the difference between the number formed by the last three digits and the number formed by the remaining digits is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, then the original number is divisible by 7, 11, or 13 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is perfectly divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 35 or 24), factorize it into co-prime factors. The number must be individually divisible by all its co-prime factors.

__
 
• **Lyophilic sols** are characterized by their strong attraction for the dispersion medium (typically water).
 
• Due to their strong affinity for the dispersion medium, lyophilic sols are **highly stable and do not coagulate easily**.
 
• They exhibit **low sensitivity** to electrolytes, unlike lyophobic sols, which are easily coagulated.
 
• Lyophilic sols **show the Tyndall effect**, which involves scattering of light by colloidal particles.
 
• Examples of lyophilic sols include **gum, gelatin, starch, and proteins**, which dissolve easily in water and form stable colloidal solutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• They are formed by substances that have a strong affinity for the dispersion medium.
 
 
 
• **Lyophobic colloids:**

• They are less stable compared to lyophilic colloids and require stabilizing agents for their preparation.
 
 
 
• **Tyndall Effect:**
 
 
• It is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, making the path of the light visible.
 
• Both lyophilic and lyophobic sols exhibit the Tyndall effect.
 
 
 
• **Coagulation:**
 
 
• It refers to the process of aggregation of colloidal particles to form larger particles, leading to precipitation.
 
• Lyophilic sols are more resistant to coagulation due to their stability.

questions.question: The average of five consecutive integers is 12. What is the largest of these integers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any arithmetic progression or sequence of consecutive integers with an odd number of terms, the average is always the exact middle term.

Since there are 5 consecutive integers, the 3rd integer (middle term) is equal to the average, which is 12.

The sequence of the five integers is: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14.

The largest integer in this sequence is 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The average of five consecutive integers is 12.

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all values ÷ Total number of values

 Average of 5 Consecutive Integers x 10 x+1 11 x+2 12 Average / Middle x+3 13 x+4 14 Largest 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the five consecutive integers be x, x + 1, x + 2, x + 3, and x + 4.

⇒ Sum of these integers = x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) + (x + 4) = 5x + 10

⇒ Average = (5x + 10) ÷ 5

⇒ Average = x + 2

⇒ We are given that the average is 12.

⇒ x + 2 = 12

⇒ x = 12 − 2 = 10

⇒ The largest integer in the series is x + 4.

⇒ Largest integer = 10 + 4 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

The average of any sequence of consecutive numbers (or an Arithmetic Progression) is always equal to (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the mathematical formula: Sum = n × (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of Even and Odd Series

The average of the first n consecutive even numbers is always (n + 1), and the average of the first n consecutive odd numbers is strictly n.

⇒ 10 ÷ 60 = [57 × (12 ÷ 60)] ÷ (57 + S)

⇒ 10 × (57 + S) = 57 × 12

⇒ 570 + 10S = 684

⇒ 10S = 684 − 570

⇒ 10S = 114

⇒ S = 11.4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 11.4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting Point Concept

If vehicles leave a point at a regular interval T, a person approaching from the opposite direction meets them at interval t. The relation is: Distance = Cab Speed × T = (Cab Speed + Person Speed) × t.

questions.question: Infant mortality rate is the number of infants per thousand who die before reaching _______ year(s) of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Infant mortality rate refers to the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• It is a critical indicator used to measure the overall health of a population, particularly maternal and child health services.
 
• The calculation of infant mortality rate is based on data collected from hospitals, birth registries, and surveys.
 
• Factors affecting infant mortality include access to healthcare, maternal nutrition, and socioeconomic conditions.
 
• Globally, organizations like WHO, UNICEF, and national health departments monitor infant mortality rates as part of public health assessment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neonatal mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of newborns within the first 28 days of life per 1,000 live births.
 
• **Postneonatal mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of infants aged 29 days to one year per 1,000 live births.
 
• **Under-five mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of children under five years of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• Countries with higher infant mortality rates often face challenges like poor healthcare infrastructure, malnutrition, and lack of sanitation.
 
• Reducing infant mortality is a key focus of international development goals, including the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being).

questions.question: Life expectancy is an indicator of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Report**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Life expectancy is a key indicator included in the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which is part of the Human Development Report published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The Human Development Report aims to measure and rank countries based on human development indicators such as life expectancy, education, and income levels.
 
• Life expectancy reflects the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on current mortality rates.
 
• It is used to assess the health and well-being of populations globally and is influenced by factors such as healthcare quality, nutrition, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• The report helps policymakers design strategies to improve living standards and address inequalities in health, education, and income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• HDI is a composite index measuring a country's average achievements in three basic aspects of human development: health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (gross national income per capita).
 
• It was introduced by the UNDP in 1990 as a measure of development beyond economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Quality of healthcare services, access to medical facilities, and advancements in medical technology.
 
• Socio-economic factors, including poverty levels, education, and sanitation.
 
• Environmental factors, such as pollution levels and availability of clean water.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• It is a critical indicator of a country’s overall health infrastructure and development.
 
• Longer life expectancy often correlates with higher levels of socio-economic development and better living conditions.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy globally has increased due to advancements in healthcare, improved nutrition, and better living conditions.
 
• However, disparities exist between high-income and low-income countries due to unequal access to resources and healthcare.

questions.question: A solid metal cylinder of height 20 cm and diameter 14 cm is melted and recast into two solid cones having volumes in the ratio 3 : 4, keeping the height 35 cm. What would be the percentage change in the flat surface area (area of the bases) before and after?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total volume is conserved. Base area is Volume ÷ Height. The volume ratio 3:4 is extra information!

⇒ Old flat area (cylinder bases) = 2 × (Volume ÷ H) = 2V ÷ H

⇒ New flat area (cone bases) = 3 × (Volume ÷ h) = 3V ÷ h

⇒ Area Ratio (New : Old) = (3 ÷ h) : (2 ÷ H) = (3 ÷ 35) : (2 ÷ 20) = 60 : 70 = 6 : 7

⇒ Decrease in flat area = 7 − 6 = 1 part

⇒ Percentage decrease = (1 ÷ 7) × 100 = 14²⁄₇%

**∴ The correct answer is 14²⁄₇% decrease.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cylinder: Radius (R) = 7 cm, Height (H) = 20 cm

Cones: Height (h) = 35 cm, Volume ratio = 3 : 4

 

 
 
 

 
• 
 R=7
 
• 
 H=20
 Old Area = 2πR²
 →
 Melted
 

 
 
• 
 
• 
 r₁
 h=35
 

 
 
• 
 
• 
 r₂
 h=35
 New Area = πr₁² + πr₂²
 Volume Ratio 3 : 4

**Step 1: Calculate Cylinder Volume**

⇒ Total Volume (V) = πR²H = π × 7² × 20 = 980π cm³

**Step 2: Calculate Cone Volumes**

⇒ Total volume is distributed in 3 : 4 ratio (Sum of parts = 7).

⇒ V₁ = (3 ÷ 7) × 980π = 420π cm³

⇒ V₂ = (4 ÷ 7) × 980π = 560π cm³

**Step 3: Calculate Base Areas (πr²) of Cones**

⇒ V₁ = ¹⁄₃ × Base Area₁ × h ⇒ 420π = ¹⁄₃ × πr₁² × 35

⇒ Base Area₁ = πr₁² = (420π × 3) ÷ 35 = 36π cm²

⇒ V₂ = ¹⁄₃ × Base Area₂ × h ⇒ 560π = ¹⁄₃ × πr₂² × 35

⇒ Base Area₂ = πr₂² = (560π × 3) ÷ 35 = 48π cm²

**Step 4: Calculate Percentage Change in Flat Area**

⇒ Old Flat Area (Top + Bottom bases) = 2 × πR² = 2 × 49π = 98π cm²

⇒ New Flat Area (Cone bases) = 36π + 48π = 84π cm²

⇒ Area Decrease = 98π − 84π = 14π cm²

⇒ Percentage Decrease = (14π ÷ 98π) × 100 = (1 ÷ 7) × 100 = 14²⁄₇%

**∴ The correct answer is 14²⁄₇% decrease.**

**__Additional Information__**

Recasting Solids Principle

When one 3D shape is melted to form another, the total volume strictly remains constant (V₁ = V₂), but the total surface area and flat surface area generally change depending on the new dimensions.

Flat Surface Area Geometry

For a solid cylinder, the flat surface consists of the top and bottom circular faces: Area = 2πr². For a solid cone, the flat surface is only the bottom circular face: Area = πr².

Volume and Base Area Relation

Both shapes have volumes proportional to their base areas. Cylinder: V = Base Area × Height. Cone: V = ¹⁄₃ × Base Area × Height. Using this relation allows direct calculation of base areas without computing actual radii.
